prompt: Use case: stylized-concept, art-direction paintover of an existing game location. Image 1 is a current in-game screenshot from the upper deck of the Mega Park in the game Yorimichi, a concrete skate park set into rugged volcanic rock in a forested valley of an island in autumn. Image 2 is another place in the same game and shows the art direction: soft painterly low-poly shapes, flat matte shading, pale lavender-grey rocks, autumn maples and ginkgos in rust, orange and gold, dark green pines, soft green grass, a clean blue sky. Repaint image 1 from exactly the same camera and composition as the improved AFTER version: the paintover a lead environment artist makes to show the team, concretely, what to change. The concrete deck, its indigo edge and the fence with its banners stay exactly as they are. The rocks become more beautiful: coherent weathered volcanic rock with clear horizontal layers and vertical joints, lighter sunlit tops and cooler shaded faces, moss and grass only on the top ledges, small maples, pines and shrubs rooted in the cracks, scree and boulders at their feet blending into the forest floor. The pale pointed rock spires and the dark rock blocks behind the fence become a beautiful group of volcanic rock pinnacles and boulders with moss, ferns and small autumn maples and pines at their feet and on their ledges. The forest round the park becomes denser and more beautiful: trees grouped in natural clumps of one species with a few small clearings, a varied canopy of different heights, a darker green understory of bushes, ferns and bamboo grass between the trunks, fallen leaves in drifts, and a soft forest edge of shrubs where the trees meet the rock and the concrete. The ground is no longer one flat green: leaf litter, darker moss under the trees, worn earth paths and grass tufts. Keep the park rugged, with a raw skate-spot character. Stay in the game's style with its low-poly leaf-card trees; do not turn it photoreal. No people, no UI, no labels, no text.
